main.content: [[File:UInpcHorde.png|frame]]'''Transmogrification''' is a custom Turtle-Wow feature that allows players to alter the appearance of their weapons and armor for a fee. It is an optional end-game system that players can choose to partake in for purely cosmetic purposes. ==Basic Concept== Transmogrification is accessible through dedicated NPCs and has two main parts: #Quest NPCs, who reward you with Fashion Coins for gathering materials, and; #Transmogrification NPCs, who let you access the Transmogrification UI. Fashion Coins (which are soulbound) are used to apply transmogrifications, each slot costing one Coin. You can acquire Fashion coins in two ways: by completing repeatable quests that involve gathering materials, or by purchasing them as a Donation Reward. The quests bump up in difficulty based on your level bracket (e.g. 20-29). ==UI == [[File:MainUI.transmog2.png|thumb|500x500px]] Transmogrification is accessed via a Fashionista NPC, located in your faction's capital city. The UI consists of two sections - your character's visible outfit on the left, and the gallery of equipment models to the right. #Outfit drop-down menu, to save the current outfit for later #Reset button #Player's character equipment #Coin balance #Apply button. Be wary - applying will irreversably spend Fashion Coins [[File:MainUI(gallery).png|thumb|500x500px]] ===Gallery === Upon picking an item to transmogrify, the menu to the right will change to show which models you have collected. #Collected models #Model tracker, which shows your total count for models in that slot ===Applying Transmogrification=== #Choose the equipment you want to transmog by clicking on its slot #Use the gallery to choose the new model you want to apply for each #Check your Coin balance, and remember that coins cannot be refunded! #Click "Apply" ===Acquiring New Models=== In order to unlock more equipment models, you must equip new items. You will then see a pop-up message that says the model was added to your collection. '''You can only save models of eqiupment that you can actually equip (i.e. keep class and faction restrictions in mind).''' The collection is also '''not''' shared across your account, instead being saved per character. ==Where to Transmogrify== === [[File:Alliance 15.png]] Alliance [[File:Alliance 15.png]] === #[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=51290 Felicia ] - Transmogrification NPC #[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=51292 Ophelia Worthington ] - Quest NPC You can find them at the '''Stormwind Fashion House''' located on the main street (Trade District), third shop to the right of the Guild Registration Office. ===[[File:Horde 15.png]] Horde [[File:Horde 15.png]]=== #[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=51291 Herrina ] - Transmogrification NPC #[https://database.turtle-wow.org/?npc=51293 Zora ] - Quest NPC Both NPCs can be found in front of the Bank in Orgrimmar. ==Quest Tiers & Requirements== All quests are repeatable for as long as player stays in their level brackets. The '''Tower of Lapidis''' is a mage tower in eastern Lapidis Isle. The tower was built by [[Arch Hydromancer Lapidis]] after the [[Kul Tiran Exploratory Fleet]] ran ground on the island through the use of Kul Tiran workers and his own water elementals. With his great power, the tower was constructed much before the town of [[Caelan's Rest]] had gotten its footing, and the Arch Hydromancer proceeded to ally himself with both the trolls of [[Zul'Hazu]] and the [[Gor'dosh Ogres]], turning on the Kul Tirans. The tower, guarded by [[Twisted Water Elemental]]s, now looms over Caelan's Rest like a great evil that could destroy them at any minute.

I offer you humble greetings, denizen of these lands.

It is remiss of me to ask this of you, but my people are in grave danger so I cannot withhold from inquiring. My name is Aneka Konko. I hail from Kamio, a land across the seas. Five years ago, we first saw the fish and snake people wash upon our shores. Their encroachments have only continued and our sacred Kami can no longer protect us.

I have arrived to this land with a small entourage to seek the help of kind souls who could assist me.

Our warriors are fighting to their last breath against the invaders, although, these days most of our warriors die not to the enemy, but to illness.

We're ill equipped to treat the many injured. Our island is small and few of us possess the knowledge or reagents needed.

When I first came here, I learned of three rare plants that possess immense healing properties. I beg of you to assist us. Retrieve these plants from the three oases in the Barrens.

Each oasis contains one of these plants.

'''Trolls''' (collectively referred to as '''trollkind''') are a diverse sapient race that can be found in every part of [[Azeroth]]. They are one of the world's oldest known native races. Trolls are divided into many subgroups adapted to different environments, namely [[Dark troll|dark trolls]], [[Forest troll|forest trolls]], [[Ice troll|ice trolls]], [[Jungle troll|jungle trolls]], [[Sand troll|sand trolls]], and [[Zandalari troll|Zandalari trolls]].

Many trolls have no loyalty except amongst their own tribes, but some important groups have joined the [[Horde]]: the [[Darkspear tribe]], [[Revantusk tribe]], and others remain independent like [[Zandalari Empire]]. Some forest trolls cling to their allegiance to the [[Old Horde]] and its [[Dark Horde|villainous offshoots]], many of them remains inside the [[Blackrock Mountain]] with the [[Dark Horde]].

=== History ===
As tribal rivalries erupted throughout the former [[Gurubashi Empire]], the Darkspear tribe found themselves driven from their homeland in [[Stranglethorn Vale]]. Having settled on the [[Darkspear islands]], which are believed today to have been a part of the [[Broken Isles]], the tribe soon found themselves entangled in a conflict with a group of [[Murloc|murlocs]]. Eventually they also found new enemies in [[Human|humans]] when a [[Kul Tiras]]-fleet landed on the island in search for some orcs who had stolen some ships. The trolls' fate seemed sealed until the orcish [[Warchief]] [[Thrall]] and his band of newly freed orcs, which were the orcs the humans were looking for, took shelter on the island after a heavy storm. The orcs managed to defeat the humans, but their victory was short-lived. Controlled by a [[Zar'jira|Sea Witch]], the [[Underworld Minions]] captured the Darkspears' leader [[Sen'jin]] along with Thrall and several orcs, trolls and humans. They were all brought to a complex prison made by caves below the island. Thrall managed to free himself and his companions, but was ultimately unable to save the trolls' leader. Although [[Sen'jin]] was sacrificed to the Sea Witch, he was able to reveal a vision he had in which Thrall would lead the Darkspear trolls from the island.

After returning to the island's surface, Thrall and his followers managed to fend off further attacks by the Sea Witch and her murloc minions, and set sail for Kalimdor once again. Under the new leadership of [[Vol'jin]], the Darkspear swore allegiance to Thrall's [[Horde]] and followed him to Kalimdor. Now considered enemies by all other troll organizations except the [[Revantusk]], [[Shatterspear]], and the [[Zandalari tribe|Zandalari]], the Darkspear are held in contempt to this day. Yet, the Darkspear have not forgotten being driven from their ancestral homes, and this animosity is eagerly returned - especially towards the other jungle trolls. Having reached and founded the orc's new homeland, [[Durotar]], the trolls carved out another home for themselves — this time among the [[Echo Isles]] on the eastern shores of the new orc kingdom.

However, with another approach by Kul Tiras and its navy, the Darkspear were forced to retreat inland under the onslaught of the misguided commander [[Daelin Proudmoore]]. The trolls, fighting alongside their Horde brethren led by the [[beastmaster]] [[Rexxar]], defeated the enemy and reclaimed their new home. Shortly thereafter, a witch doctor by the name of [[Zalazane]] began using dark magic to take the minds of his fellow Darkspear. As his army of mindless followers grew, Vol'jin ordered the free trolls to evacuate, and Zalazane took control of the Echo Isles. The Darkspear have since settled on the nearby shore, naming their new village after their old leader, Sen'jin. From [[Sen'jin Village]] they, along with their allies, send forces to battle Zalazane and his enslaved army.

=== Appearance ===
The appearance of Trolls varies depending on their type and tribe to which they belong:

'''Jungle Trolls:''' The most common currently, they usually live on islands, they are organized into tribes like any other type of trolls, of which the Blackspear Tribe formally belongs to the Horde, with bluish skin and elongated arms and legs with muscles for the males.

Troll females have a build more similar to the other races, however, the bluish skin with some warts on the skin remains.

Both genders have two protruding tusks, with those of the males being more prominent. Some use war paint and certain wings on their fangs or any other area of the face.

'''Forest Trolls:''' The second most common type of Troll to see, they tend to reside in forested areas, they have a long history of war with the High Elves and with the human race over the lands of Quel'thalas and Lordaeron that are now under the domain of the plague, with a somewhat different constitution and with an easily recognizable pigmentation on the skin, being green, but very similar to the Jungle trolls, previously the Amani Trolls belonged to the Old Horde, currently only the Revantusk tribe has joined her.

'''Ice Trolls:''' They are a type of trolls that reside in cold areas similar to their other congeners, they only differ in the light blue pigmentation of their skin, probably due to the icy climates in which they live. They can be easily seen in the most distant areas of Dun Morogh.

'''Sand Trolls:''' A type of Troll difficult to see in the Eastern Kingdoms, residing in the distant lands of Kalimdor, in Tanaris, they are an aggressive type of Troll, they will rarely be seen being friendly with others other than their own. tribe, pigmented with a color similar to the yellowish sand due to the hot climate of the desert and with customs even more primitive than the other types of Troll, often perform dark rituals in honor of their ancient gods in the depths of the ruins of Zul 'farrak.

'''Zandalari Trolls:''' A special tribe of Trolls and the most civilized of all, the Zandalari Trolls come from the Far Island of Zandalar, the last bastion of the once great Zandalari empire, they are currently in Stranglethorn Valley trying to stop the invocation to the current plane of the Blood God Hakkar by the Hakkari and their loyalists within Zul'gurub and the Temple of Atal'Hakkar.

'''Dark Trolls:''' The most difficult type of Troll to see in all of Azeroth, of currently unknown origin and scattered in small tribes throughout the world, their pigmentation is dark purple, they tend to practice arcane magic and witchcraft, there are those who say that they have some kind of relationship with the Night Elves.

'''Tofvic Arkenbrine''' or simply ''''Vic'''<nowiki/>', is a Lordaeronian witch hunter who serves as the current Keeper of Hawk's Talon after the death of Heralt, the original keeper.

== '''<small>Appearance and Personality</small>''' ==
Tofvic is a physically imposing man in his mid 40s, sporting graying facial hair that was originally black, and a bald head. He stands at an average-tall human height of 182,5 cm (6'0" ft). His skin, kissed by sun and wind, bears a light tan. His small brown eyes, sharp and watchful, resemble those of a hawk. Thin, low eyebrows frame his gaze. His head is cleanly shaved, revealing a smooth scalp. His face resembles a shield coated in leather.

Tofvic is a pragmatic and disciplined man, shaped by years of hardship and moral conflict. His experiences have left him with a sharp sense of justice, tempered by a deep understanding of the complexities of good and evil. He is often quiet and reflective, preferring action over words. Despite his stern demeanor, Tofvic harbors a deep compassion for the innocent and will go to great lengths to protect them. He is willing to bend rules when the greater good demands it but remains firm in his convictions about the dangers of unchecked magic and corruption.

==Profile==
===Background===
[[File:Kid Tofvic.jpg|left|thumb|210x210px|Tofvic as a child wandering the streets of Hearthglen.]]
Tofvic was born into a middle class family in the peaceful region of Hearthglen. His father was a respected treasurer. From an early age, he displayed a deep curiosity about the nature of existence and the forces that governed it. Often pondering the interplay of good and evil, he felt drawn to the divine teachings of the Light, which spoke of justice, compassion, and order. Seeking a greater understanding of these ideals, Tofvic left his home as a teenager to train as a cleric in The Old Monastery, which is now known as the Scarlet Monastery.

After the Second War, Tofvic sought to expand his role beyond the priesthood, embracing the desire to protect and defend. Driven by this conviction, he began rigorous training to become a paladin, blending his spiritual discipline with martial prowess. This transition marked a pivotal chapter in his journey.

=== A New Threat ===
Though the Alliance prevailed in the Second War, peace was fleeting. As the years passed, a new darkness emerged: the undead Scourge. The plague that swept through the land turned friends and family into enemies, reducing entire towns to lifeless husks. Tofvic, now a seasoned paladin in his 30s, joined the desperate efforts to combat the spreading corruption, wielding the Light to strike down countless undead and shield the innocent from harm.

Yet, even with the might of the Light, its limitations became increasingly apparent. His recent experiences on the battlefield left Tofvic questioning not the power of the Light itself, but the constraints of relying solely on it—especially in a world where threats grew ever larger and more relentless with each passing day.

===A New Path===
Seeking answers to bridge these gaps, Tofvic retreated into solitude. He traveled to the secluded mountains of Khaz Modan, where he immersed himself in texts from various disciplines. Through his study and reflection, Tofvic came to a profound realization: the forces of Light and Shadow, often depicted as opposing absolutes, might instead be facets of a greater truth. Each held strengths and weaknesses, and together they could offer a path to true balance and understanding.

Tofvic’s newfound philosophy reshaped his approach to justice and compassion. He remained devoted to ways of the Light and order but came to understand the Shadow as a tool to address what the Light could not. He understood that wielding Shadow came with risks. The temptation to delve deeper or use it carelessly could corrupt the unprepared. His training as a paladin, however, had instilled in him discipline and unwavering willpower, enabling him to walk this precarious path without faltering.

Tofvic’s transformation into a Discipline Priest marked his departure from the rigid structure of the paladin. He set aside his plate armor and embraced a new path that demanded constant vigilance and self-control. He trained himself to wield both Light and Shadow responsibly, using each force to counter the other and maintain equilibrium. However, his unorthodox philosophy was often deemed heretical by traditional clerics of the Light, leading him to distance himself from any formal order aligned with the Holy Light.  

=== Keeper of the Talon ===
[[File:Ellennya Arkenbrine.jpg|left|thumb|250x250px|Ellennya Arkenbrine, Tofvic's wife]]
Tofvic eventually reunited with his wife, Ellennya Arkenbrine, a skilled herbalist from Lordaeron who had sought refuge in Menethil Harbor. Together, they moved south to Duskwood, a region steeped in darkness and plagued by malevolent forces. Drawing on his harrowing experiences during the plague of Lordaeron and his deep understanding of the corrupting nature of dark magic, Tofvic devoted himself to hunt the undead, cursed creatures, and practitioners of forbidden arts to purify the world with justice. He firmly believed that such dangerous knowledge should be wielded only by those with unwavering faith and a strict adherence to order. This unyielding pursuit of justice and purification earned him a reputation as a steadfast witch hunter.

During a mission to investigate a growing dark magic threat in a nearby village, Tofvic encountered a group of witch hunters known as the Hawk's Talon, a faction dedicated to eradicating chaotic forces that threaten the world. Together, they joined forces to track down the source of the dark magic. Their investigation led to a fateful clash with a powerful sorceress.

Recognizing the alignment of their goals and the strength of their resolve, Tofvic officially joined the Hawks' Talon. His membership marked a new chapter in his quest to combat the forces of darkness, this time as part of a more structured and disciplined order. He was entrusted with the role of Keeper, where he is responsible for the overall management and operation of the guild. He and Ellennya moved to Hawk's Vigil in Dun Agrath and currently lives there.

== Enemies ==

=== Joseph Shadowbrine ===
[[File:Shadowbrine.jpg|thumb|220x220px|left]]
Once ''Joseph Wenzel'', Shadowbrine is a Forsaken warlock and leader of the Shadowspire Cult, a ruthless and secretive sect devoted to the worship of demons. The cult sees themselves as the chosen architects of a new age where demons reign supreme. Their rituals are dark and brutal, often involving blood sacrifices of newborn childs and the corruption of sacred grounds. A childhood bully and former classmate of Tofvic Arkenbrine, Joseph’s hunger for power led him to embrace the dark arts and corruption.

While investigating the cult's activities, Tofvic discovered their leader was Joseph himself. The confrontation between the two was inevitable. The ensuing battle was fierce, a clash of faith against corruption. Tofvic, despite his resolve, struggled against Shadowbrine’s cunning and his mastery of demonic pacts.

In the end, Tofvic prevailed, delivering a decisive blow to his former classmate. Seeing no path to redemption for a man so steeped in evil, he ended Joseph’s life. He left the warlock’s body to rot amidst the desecrated ruins of the cult’s sanctuary. However, Joseph’s story did not end there. His corpse was discovered by Forsaken scavengers and brought to Tirisfal Glades, where he was reanimated. The resurrection amplified his bitterness and hatred.

=== Zaraphina Duskwatch ===
[[File:Zaraphina.jpg|thumb|220x220px|left]]
Zaraphina was once Tofvic’s loyal companion and apprentice. Together, they fought to purge darkness and protect the innocent, their bond forged through shared struggles. Over time, however, the relentless battles took their toll. Zaraphina grew disillusioned, questioning whether the Light alone could ever bring victory against the ever-growing threats in a changing world. Her doubts only deepened as she witnessed Tofvic’s use of Shadow—a practice she struggled to accept. 

After a devastating mission in Duskwood, Zaraphina departed under the pretense of seeking clarity. In truth, she turned to forbidden magic, desperate to find a solution to the world’s chaos. Her descent into fel magic transformed her into a ruthless warlock, convinced that power, not balance, was the key to saving their homeland. Zaraphina’s betrayal shattered Tofvic’s trust, leaving him to grapple with the painful loss of his apprentice—and the formidable new threat she had become.

The '''Troll Wars''' were a series of conflicts between the [[forest troll]]s of [[Zul'Aman]] and an alliance between the [[human]]s of [[Arathor]] and [[high elf|high elves]] of [[Quel'Thalas]], occurring approximately 2,800 years before the coming of the [[orc]]s to [[Azeroth]].

The war started because the [[High Elves]] founded the kingdom of [[Quel'Thalas]] over the trolls' sacred ground. There once lay an ancient troll city that was in ruins because of unknown reason.  Elven magic helped to frighten away the superstitious troll warbands and 4,000 years passed before the trolls started the real war.

The human tribes, also suffering at the hands of the trolls, finally banded together to form the first human nation of [[Arathor]]. After countless years of being continually besieged by the native trolls, the high elves of eventually sought the aid of the humans of Arathor. The two nations formed an alliance, in which the elves taught the humans the art of magic in exchange for military aid. 

The now strengthened alliance of high elves and humans eventually defeated the forest trolls so completely that the race would never fully recover in the [[Eastern Kingdoms]].
